As many of yall know, Shamat is the combined continents of East, and West Shamat.

Although differences are present, people from Shamat always have had a feeling of a bond with each other, especially compared to their connections with other continents. Neo-Colonialism is still present at all current times, and people usually don't like those nations being present on their continents, some exceptions are very much present, but there will always be a feeling of external influences.

50 years ago, something ignited, something started, in a lot of forms and identities, but it was still unknown, [i]sadly[/i]. Many forms and versions existed, you can call them what you want; left, right, progressive, conservative, extreme, centrist and beyond. Even people from Shamat, who were outside Shamat, felt a connection to this idea, to this concept.

It grew and it grew, at some point every single person in a city would know about it. The Idea of Shamatism and/or Pan-Shamatism. BUT, the problem was, no one was truly expressing it yet, and no one truly saw it as something doable. Until one certain day in the Sikirskian province of Zirsk, to be precise, in the now-very-important city of [b]Kerlgrad:[/b]

[b]-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[b]A Congress![/b]

I have recently founded the Sikirskian Pan-Shamatist Salvation Party, and as planned it has grown to a national scale. I see many of you here, from the Far East, to the Far West.

[b][i]Pan-Shamatism - A Novel Idea[/i][/b]

Pan-Shamatism as a concept may have existed in the minds of Dhora philosophers for a long time but to the rulers of Dhornaper, whose empires stretched far and wide, the idea was a bastardisation of their natural inheritance: the entirety of the Shamats. Pan-Shamatism meant the rule of the Dhora Shahs over all of both Shamats.

However, after the collapse of the last great Dhora Empire, the concept was rediscovered but again, not as a means to unify the Shamats for collective strength but as a cunning political objective to prevent colonial powers intruding on Dhornaper's backyard.

Since the general collapse of colonialism, with some exceptions, the concept was forgotten. Today, most of Dhornaper's population does not hold strong feelings of belonging with other Shamatine nations. A sizeable chunk even consider Dhornaper as above the other Shamatine nations by right of its history and culture. Previous governments weren't interested, however, the current government sees Pan-Shamatism as something worth entertaining. Should it succeed, the government does not want to be left out. Should it fail, the government will gain some measure of respect for attempting such a grand project to unify and develop weaker Shamatine nations, so it thinks. No matter the outcome, the government of President Fereydun Khan is interested, at least for now, and has applied to join the Shamatine Security Pact, the only currently existing Pan-Shamatine international organisation.
